title: UIC stabbing: Student arrested in attempted crime at UIC Student Center East on Halsted; FBI, ATF investigating
text:
UIC stabbing: Suspect attempted to use 'incendiary device' at UIC Student Center East on Halsted before trying to stab student - ABC7 Chicago

 Suspect attempted to use 'incendiary device' at UIC before trying to stab fellow student: officials 
 FBI, ATF investigating; student center to reopen Thursday; witness said attacker had butcher knife 
 The FBI and ATF are investigating after an attempted stabbing at UIC. WLS By Leah Hope Thursday, November 5, 2026 2:14AM Share CHICAGO (WLS) -- A student was arrested Wednesday for allegedly attempting to use an "incendiary device" before trying to stab another student on campus, University of Illinois Chicago officials said.
 At about 12:39 p.m. UIC sent an alert urging people to avoid the UIC Student Center East building at 750 S. Halsted St.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 A student allegedly tried to stab another student on the second floor, a UIC spokesperson said.
 Before the attempted stabbing, the "individual attempted to use an incendiary device in a second-floor hallway of SCE," officials said in an update Wednesday evening.
 The suspect was taken into custody.
 The victim was not injured, UIC said.
 Student Center East was evacuated and remains closed as police continue to investigate.
 UIC said there is no threat to the campus community.
 The FBI said it is aware of the incident and is supporting the investigation along with several other law enforcement agencies.
 The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is also on the scene.
 Two students said two of their roommates were targeted. They shared what they say their roommates told them about the attack that came out of the blue.
 "Somebody threw a bottle. It went straight past his face, and then he turned, saw dude pull out the butcher knife, and took off," Kaleb Miller said.

 Someone fell trying to get away, they said.
 "He slipped on some liquid from the bottle. And before he knew it, he was getting attacked. And the guy tried to stab him multiple times. So he continued to kick his feet, kicks his, and eventually he hit the guy in the jaw. The attacker started to stumble back, and then he was able to get up and run away," Jonathan Uribe said.
 Others spoke about what they saw.
 "I heard some commotion. And when I turned it around, I saw all the people on the floor, and then the police were there. And they're like yelling at the guy to get on the floor and everything. And then it was like a lot going on; so I didn't really like know what was going on," Simon Dean said.
 "What raised the red flag ... was we seen three to four or five officers backing up, clutching the weapons. And then next thing you know, we hear a scream, saying, 'Get out, get out, and get out the way,'" EJ Johnson said.
 Students shared images of what they saw.

 Some described seeing a man on the ground and that man being arrested.
 "I feel like everything's being kind of handled right. I mean, you know, they evacuated us out. There's nothing really we can do. I just think it's always like, 'hurry up and wait,' trying to figure out, you know, what's really happening," Nicole Donnelly said.
 Some students said they hope access is restricted to only students to keep the building safer.
 "You know, people can just come in, and stuff like that can happen. But you know, you never really think it would happen. So I'm not really sure how to feel about it," Eric Landicho said.
 "I hate what happened here today. You know, I just wish the campus was a bit more safer a little bit, so you know we don't have to necessarily worry about this stuff," Osei Boakye said.
 The student center is expected to reopen at 6:30 a.m. Thursday, after school officials gave the all clear.
